description: Gold closes 2025 up roughly 64% for the year after breaching USD 3,000 and USD 4,000 for the first time. Record annual gold ETF inflows of about USD 89bn.
primary_transmission: Gold, precious metals miners, inflation hedges

description: Spot gold trades above USD 5,000 per ounce for the first time.
Gold prints an intraday all-time high near USD 5,589 per ounce, then begins a multi-month consolidation.
United States and Israel commence military operations against Iran.
primary_transmission: Energy, defence, airlines, EM credit, safe havens

description: Brent crude rises 10-13% to around USD 80-82 per barrel as tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz stalls and a major Saudi refinery shuts down.
Strait of Hormuz effectively closed. Brent surges past USD 120. QatarEnergy declares force majeure on all exports.
primary_transmission: Energy, LNG, shipping, Gulf credit, airlines

description: IEA member countries agree to release 400 million barrels from emergency reserves.
IEA characterises the conflict as the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market, with roughly 7.5% of world supply affected.
European Central Bank and several other central banks raise policy rates in response to an energy-driven inflation impulse.
Brent crude peaks at approximately USD 114 per barrel.
Megacap technology complex briefly sheds around USD 2 trillion in market value on AI capital expenditure concerns before recovering later in the month.
primary_transmission: US technology, concentrated equity, collateralised lending

description: Federal Reserve holds the target range at 3.50-3.75% at the first meeting under new Chair Kevin Warsh. Easing timeline pushed out.
US 10-year Treasury yield rises to about 4.46%, near its highest level in more than a year.
Half-year close. US equities near record levels on narrow, technology-led leadership. Non-traded private credit vehicles show continued redemption stress.
Federal Reserve holds again at 3.50-3.75% with three dissents. US 10-year yield reaches 4.71% by month end. Market pricing shifts from cuts toward possible hikes.
United States reimposes a naval blockade following renewed Iranian attacks on commercial vessels. Energy risk premium re-widens.
